paragraphs: Job asks the question that sits under this whole passage: "how can a mortal be righteous before God?" (Job 9:2). He looks at how mighty God is and feels like he could never win an argument with Him, and friend, I can't even win one with my own oven timer. Then he says what he's missing: there is no "mediator between us" (Job 9:33). Job is telling us how far away God feels to him, and he says it plainly.

Here's what I love, friend. Job doesn't just smile and say he's fine, though he pictures doing it and says he would still dread all his sufferings (Job 9:27-28). You know that "I'm good, all good" text you send while you are NOT good? Job skips it. He says, "I will express my complaint" (Job 10:1), and he takes it straight to God, not around Him: "I will say to God" (Job 10:2).

In the middle of the hurt, Job still remembers who made him. He says, "Your hands shaped me and altogether formed me" (Job 10:8), and that God's "care has preserved my spirit" (Job 10:12). So when you're hurting, you can bring God the honest version, the messy one, and keep talking to Him. Some of Job's words in this passage are heavy, and he leaves us in the dark, but the story isn't over.
